calls.head: Special teams tilt toward Dallas
calls.body: Dallas’s power play creates 8.7 expected goals per 60, 3rd in the league. San Jose’s penalty kill ranks 24th.
calls.call: Dallas’s power play creates at least its usual 8.7 expected goals per 60.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Dallas’s power play created 10.7 expected goals per 60 in 6:00 of 5-on-4 time, against its usual 8.7, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: Expect a grind
calls.body: San Jose’s games average only 79.5 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (26th of 32 for pace); Dallas’s average 75.6 (32nd).
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than the two teams’ usual 77.6 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 60.1 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 77.6 and a league average of 82.0.

DAL.head: We gave Dallas a 61% chance, and Dallas delivered.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose only a 39% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Dallas leaned on its bottom six
surprises.body: Dallas’s bottom-six forwards played 45% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against its usual 40% and a league average of 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 50 games.

surprises.head: Dallas buried San Jose in shots
surprises.body: Dallas took 70% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Dallas would expect about 53%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 90 games.
